analysis:
On 27 September 2013 Rahul Gandhi, then Congress vice-president, told a press conference that the ordinance on convicted lawmakers was "complete nonsense" and should be "torn up and thrown away". The ordinance had been promulgated to negate the Supreme Court's 10 July 2013 ruling in Lily Thomas v. Union of India, which held that a legislator convicted and sentenced to two years or more loses membership with immediate effect.

The Union Cabinet withdrew both the ordinance and the accompanying bill on 2 October 2013, five days after his remarks. The Supreme Court's ruling remained in force, and Rasheed Masood became the first MP disqualified under it on 1 October 2013.

In 2019 Rahul Gandhi told Hindustan Times that he had possibly expressed himself "too aggressive"ly on that occasion.
notes: The press conference is reported as 27 September 2013 by The Hindu and Rediff and as 28 September 2013 by some outlets; 27 September is used. The Business Line withdrawal article URL was identified through the Wikipedia reference list.
